outcomes: Compute scaled causal query-key scores and probability-weighted values
Explain queries, keys, and values by role and shape
Derive manual gradients for Q, K, V, and row softmax
Distinguish an attention derivative probe from next-token cross-entropy
Use finite differences and causal invariance as complementary tests

self-attention.name: self-attention
self-attention.definition: A content-dependent weighted mixture whose queries, keys, and values come from the same sequence.
self-attention.explanation: Each query row scores key rows, row softmax converts scores to source-position probabilities, and the weighted sum retrieves value rows. Scores are scaled by the inverse square root of head width to control predictable dot-product growth. Self-attention exchanges information across positions, unlike a feed-forward layer that transforms positions independently. Multiple heads repeat the calculation on feature slices. The operation does not by itself enforce sequence direction; a causal mask supplies that restriction for autoregressive language modeling.

causal-mask.name: causal mask
causal-mask.definition: A restriction that permits position i to attend only to positions j where j is not later than i.
causal-mask.explanation: During parallel next-token training, future tokens are present in the input tensor. Without a causal mask, a representation can read information about the target it must predict, producing misleadingly low loss. Mask forbidden attention scores before row softmax so their source-position probability and score gradient are zero. These probabilities choose input positions; they are distinct from the later probability distribution over predicted token classes. The diagonal is allowed because position i contains the current input token while its target is token i+1.

gradient-check.name: gradient check
gradient-check.definition: A comparison between an analytical derivative and a numerical finite-difference estimate.
gradient-check.explanation: For a scalar objective P and input element θ, central difference estimates the derivative as [P(θ+ε)−P(θ−ε)]/(2ε). It is slow but useful on tiny deterministic fixtures. Smooth inputs, suitable precision, and combined absolute and relative tolerances matter. This chapter sums attention outputs times a fixed upstream matrix to create a derivative probe; that probe is not a model loss or next-token cross-entropy. Causal invariance and shape tests complement numerical derivatives because agreement alone cannot prove the intended information flow.

sources.title: Attention Is All You Need
sources.note: Original scaled dot-product and multi-head attention source.

checks: causal_attention receives direct row-major query, key, and value arrays and returns output plus source-position probabilities with the documented shapes
Every Q, K, and V element passes f64 central differences against the summed attention_probe_objective
backward propagates supplied output gradients without an extra averaging denominator
Future key and value changes cannot affect earlier outputs, and masked probabilities are exactly zero
Default run traces probabilities, outputs, and nonzero gradient norms
limitations: The standalone project receives direct Q, K, and V inputs rather than token IDs or learned projections
It implements one attention head and no dropout
Its test-only probe objective is not next-token cross-entropy
Quadratic attention storage is suitable only for short sequences
